newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher after Monday's rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher after Monday's rally.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Tuesday after rallying Monday on the return of hot, dry weather in the Southwest and firmer spot physical prices across the West.

In early over-the-counter business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $29.75-29.90 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Monday's settlement of $29.29, while the July California-Oregon Border (COB) contract was discussed at $19.40-19.70 against yesterday's close of $19.33.
On ACCESS, July COB finished at $19.30, down three cents from yesterday's settlement but July PV was inactive.
Concerns over reduced Northwest power supply to southern California this summer continued to put some upward pressure on the complex, market sources said.
A Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is expected to introduce a proposal later this week to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system in early July.
The plan called for a summertime rating for the intertie at 6,900 megawatt (MW) from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
In the meantime, Bonneville Power Administration said last week the summer transmission capacity on the intertie be reduced to 6,300, down 900 MW from current level.

Some hydropower projects in the Northwest are struggling to deal with near-record runoff volumes this spring, but the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which operates most the region's hydroelectric dams, told Reuters it expects the situation to improve this summer.

While forecasts of triple-digit temperatures in the interior part of the Southwest through next week would keep the region's air-conditioning demand strong, the Northwest would experience cooler-than-normal spring weather.

More coal-fired generation is slated to return online from maintenance outages and repair shutdowns. A 190 megawatt (MW) Four Corners unit in New Mexico and a 750 MW Mohave unit in Nevada are scheduled to restart today.
Moreover, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state is expected to resume output later this week.
